conviction_note: The primary documents put the Q3 revenue and EPS consensus at or a little under the middle of what the July guide and backlog conversion imply, so the quarter itself carries a slight beat lean (+0.5). The negatives (CEO open-window selling at $600-637, a bookings gain that management credited to lower cancellations rather than gross wins, pass-through-heavy growth, a stock at its 52-week high after an 8% five-day run with +11.9 vol points of put skew and shorts already covered) add up to impact_sum -1.7. On the scaled side, abs_move is 12.5 (implied 11.2, own median 14.7, on a name that trades on book-to-bill) and p_up is 47, which gives -0.75. Both measurements lean slightly negative and neither rests on a number the market has not seen. The search budget ran out after four searches, so peer prints and Q3 biotech funding went unchecked.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus about $4.44 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MEDP/earnings-forecasts) and $4.45 (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/MEDP): two sources that agree. Revenue consensus is $713.2M (Benzinga) against $708.75M and $694.23M in two Earnings Whispers snapshots, so the revenue bar is disputed. Company guide (8-K 2026-07-22, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001668397/000166839726000023/medp-2026722exx991.htm): FY2026 revenue $2.805-2.885B, EPS $17.25-17.95. After H1 revenue of $1,413.9M and EPS of $8.53, that implies H2 revenue of $1,391-1,471M ($696-736M a quarter) and H2 EPS of $8.72-9.42 ($4.36-4.71 a quarter). Consensus EPS sits below the midpoint of that implied range. The trade turns on net new business awards and book-to-bill, and no sourced consensus exists for those; Q2 was 1.13x and Q3 2025 was 1.20x. Consensus figures are search snippets only.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.6M shares at FINRA settlement 2026-09-30, 5.8 days to cover, about 5.7% of shares outstanding (about 7% of float excluding Troendle's 19.1%), down from a 2.2M peak on 2026-07-15. Source: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/medp/short-interest/ (fetched 2026-10-21). This is not a crowded short, and with shorts already covered there is little squeeze fuel. The 25-delta skew is +11.91 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI is 0.73, the event-implied move is 11.17%, and spot of $665.96 sits at the 52-week high (+69% off the low) after +8.0% in 5 days and +7.9% in 20 days.

findings.finding: Q3 consensus sits inside, and at or below the middle of, what the company's own July guide and backlog conversion imply. Q1 and Q2 converted 23.3% and 24.1% of opening backlog, which on the $3,014.2M June 30 backlog gives about $702-726M of Q3 revenue against a $708-713M consensus. The FY guide less H1 gives $696-736M a quarter. On EPS, guide less H1 ($8.53) gives $4.36-4.71 a quarter against a $4.44-4.45 consensus. Q3 also carries the full-quarter share count effect of the 705,616 shares bought back in April-May at an average $417.70, none in June.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Medpace's reactions have followed bookings, not revenue or EPS beats. Q1 2026 grew revenue 26.5% with EPS of $4.28 and the stock fell 22.6% on a 0.88x book-to-bill. Q2 2026 printed 1.13x and rose 14.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The arithmetic is public, and a consensus far below the guide midpoint would have looked different. What is left is a small beat-and-raise lean, because consensus EPS is in the lower half of the guide-implied range and the share count effect of the Q2 buyback is mechanical. It lands inside the guided range.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000166839726000017/medp-20260422exx991.htm) and the Q2 10-Q's issuer-purchase table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000166839726000025/medp-20260630.htm) are company documents. The consensus figures come from aggregator snippets.

findings.finding: Per a MarketBeat summary of the Q2 call, management credited most of Q2's improvement in net awards ($795.7M, +28.2% y/y, 1.13x) to fewer cancellations rather than higher gross bookings. Q3 compares against Q3 2025 net awards of $789.6M (1.20x). To repeat about 1.1x on roughly $710M of revenue, Q3 needs about $780M of net awards, roughly flat y/y, and lower cancellations are a less repeatable source of that than gross wins.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Book-to-bill is the line this stock trades on: 0.88x gave -22.6% (2026-04-22), 1.13x gave +14.7% (2026-07-22), 1.20x gave +9.1% (2025-10-22), and the 2025-07-21 print moved +54.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock has rerated to the 52-week high since July on the 1.13x print, which suggests the market extrapolates the bookings recovery. If the cancellation-driven quality of that recovery were priced, the post-Q2 run would have faded rather than extended (+8% in the last 5 days). This is snippet only: the fetch returned an index page, not the article.
findings.independence: The Q2 10-Q MD&A says only that 'cancellations arise in the normal course of business' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000166839726000025/medp-20260630.htm), so no second source confirms the cancellation attribution.

findings.finding: CEO, President and 19.1% holder August Troendle sold shares on the open market under limit orders from 2026-08-10 through 2026-09-30 at about $600-637. The sales were not under a 10b5-1 plan (Form 4 checkbox 0; footnote: 'limit order placed during an open trading window'). The latest Form 4 shows 26,701 shares sold on 09-29 at $621.02 and 21,966 on 09-30 at $625.47, leaving 338,225 shares direct and 4,733,019 through Medpace Investors LLC. He has also been acting President since Jesse Geiger left on 2026-05-31.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release-level history ties these sales to a reaction. This is Schedule 13D Amendment No. 24, so Troendle has sold repeatedly through past prints, both up and down.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The filings are public and the selling is habitual, which is why this is sized small. What is left is that the selling was discretionary, inside the quarter, by the executive who now also runs operations as President, and that it stopped at quarter-end (consistent with a window closing). The market would have reacted to it if it were new behaviour.
findings.independence: Schedule 13D/A No. 24, event date 2026-09-24 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000119312526405684/0001193125-26-405684.txt): same person, a separate filing listing sales from Aug 10 to Sep 25. The Form 4 and the 13D/A describe one selling program, so they are counted once here.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q discloses a securities class action (filed 2026-04-06) and a derivative suit (filed 2026-06-22), both over the company's book-to-bill statements. That puts extra scrutiny on how the bookings and cancellation figures are presented on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The suits followed the -22.6% reaction to Q1 2026, and the stock rose 14.7% on Q2 despite them.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced as a litigation item. It bears on this print only if the disclosure of cancellations changes, and nothing indicates that it will.

findings.finding: Growth is pass-through heavy. Reimbursed out-of-pocket expenses were $303.1M of Q2's $707.3M revenue (43%). Service revenue, revenue less reimbursed costs, was $404.2M, +10.5% y/y against $365.8M in Q2 2025, while reported revenue grew 17.2%. Year to date, reimbursed costs are $615.1M against $439.9M (+40%). A top-line beat made of pass-throughs is a lower-quality beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 grew revenue 26.5%, with reimbursed costs of $312.0M against $202.4M, and the stock fell 22.6%. That suggests headline revenue strength alone does not hold the stock up.
findings.why_not_priced: The split is in the release, but consensus is quoted on total revenue. If the market priced service revenue, the revenue snapshots would not vary by $19M across sources.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000166839726000017/medp-20260422exx991.htm) shows the same pattern. This finding shares the Q2 release with finding 1.

findings.finding: Spot is $665.96 at the 52-week high, +8.0% in 5 days and +7.9% in 20 days, about 59% above the company's own Q2 buyback average of $417.70 (it made no June purchases and has $527M left). 25-delta skew is +11.91 vol points toward puts, and short interest fell from 2.2M (Jul 15) to 1.6M (Sep 30). The pre-print run leaves the bar high on bookings, and there is little short fuel to cushion a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 4 of the last 7 prints fell (-22.6, -15.9, -7.5, -2.3), and the two biggest drops came after a run-up into strong prior quarters. The median absolute move is 14.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction agrees with the skew, so the options market already leans this way. The finding is that the equity has run into the print against that skew, which is a demanding setup. Sized small because it agrees with what the options price.
findings.independence: The issuer-purchase table in the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000166839726000025/medp-20260630.htm) shows the company bought at about $408-420 and stopped in June.

findings.finding: EVP Operations Susan Burwig exercised 2,000 options (2026-10-07) and 3,000 options (2026-10-12) at $166.73 and filed no sale, taking her direct holding to 70,984 shares. The options expire on 2026-10-27, so the exercise is driven by expiry.
findings.why_not_priced: Barely informative. The only signal is that the exercised shares were not sold into the high in the days before the print.
findings.independence: Earlier exercise on the Form 4 filed 2026-10-09 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1668397/000167741826000012/0001677418-26-000012.txt), same person.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the +11.9 vol-point put skew and cuts against the run-up: the stock ran 8% into a print whose decisive line, bookings, is unknowable from public data, and the slight beat lean on revenue and EPS sits inside the guide.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the Troendle selling is habitual (13D Amendment 24), so it went from -0.7 to -0.4.
Rule 3: the class action is a known litigation item with no path to this print's numbers, so it went from -0.2 to -0.1.
The pessimism artefact ('asking what the market missed generates pessimism'): p_up moved from 46 to 47, and expected_move_pct from -1.0 to -0.75.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): EPS consensus has two agreeing sources and the company guide brackets it. Revenue consensus is disputed, so the reported-quarter findings stay small. No change.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest was checked (5.7% of shares out, not crowded). The negative agrees with the skew. No change.
Rule 1 (reaction function): bookings, not EPS, drive this name, so the beat lean stays at +0.5. No change.
